paper.title: Phase transformation and austenite stability during thermomechanical processing of high (~5%) Al added low-density medium Mn steel
paper.paper_scope: A high (~5 wt.%) Al added low-density medium Mn steel (Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C, measured Fe-7.79Mn-4.88Al-0.84Si-0.2C) was developed via melting-casting, hot forging, hot rolling+water quenching, and intercritical annealing at 750°C for 5-180 min; the work correlates thermomechanical processing and annealing time with phase transformation (delta ferrite, martensite, reverted austenite, intercritical ferrite), austenite mechanical stability, and tensile/work-hardening behavior (TRIP effect).

alloys.alloy_name: Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) high Al added low-density medium Mn steel
aliases: Al added low density medium Mn steel
low-density high Al (~5 wt.%) added medium Mn steel
alloys.description: Low-density medium Mn steel designed with a high Al addition (~5 wt.%) to reduce density; developed by the conventional melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace. The high Al and Si stabilize delta ferrite whereas Mn and C stabilize austenite.
alloys.alloys_notes: Designed/nominal composition is Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%). The final measured composition (XRF and OES, Table 1) is Fe-7.79Mn-4.88Al-0.84Si-0.2C (wt.%) with P 0.03 and S 0.03 wt.%. Measured density 6.91455 g/cc (~11.35% lower than conventional steel ~7.8 g/cc). Theoretical SFE of the designed steel ~35 mJ/m².

source.reason: The paper designs and develops one steel: 'the proposed/designed Al added low density Fe-8Mn-5Al-0.2C (wt.%) medium Mn steel' [b0014]. Its final measured composition (Table 1) is Fe bal., Mn 7.79, Al 4.88, Si 0.84, C 0.2, P 0.03, S 0.03 wt.% [b0016]. The conclusion restates the developed steel as Fe-7.79Mn-4.88Al-0.84Si-0.2C [b0075]. The designed and measured compositions refer to the same single alloy, hence defined once.

processes.description: As-solidified cast ingot produced by the melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnace, air cooled to room temperature; dual-phase delta ferrite + austenite (dendritic austenite) microstructure.

source.reason: The developed steel was produced 'by melting-casting route in an open-air induction furnance' [b0014]; the cast specimen is characterized (XRD/optical) as a dual-phase delta ferrite + austenite with dendritic austenite [b0036]. This is the first studied state.

processes.description: Cast ingot homogenized at 1100°C for 2 h, then hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800°C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.
processes.processes_notes: Dilatometry was additionally performed on the hot-forged specimen [b0018], but that is a characterization test rather than a distinct state.

source.reason: The cast ingot 'has been homogenized at 1100°C for 2hr and hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range of 1050-800°C following air cooling to room temperature' [b0014]. The hot forged specimen is characterized as a distinct studied state [b0036, b0037].

processes.description: Hot forged sample hot rolled (soaking 1100°C, 2 h) in the temperature range 1050-800°C in two passes (reheating at 1100°C for 5 min between passes) with 50% thickness reduction in each pass, followed by water quenching to room temperature from the finish rolling temperature (~800°C).
processes.processes_notes: Converts part of the austenite to lenticular martensite due to the high cooling rate (water quenching); remaining austenite is termed untransformed austenite. Also referred to as 'hot rolled' in Table 3.

source.reason: Hot forged samples 'have been further hot rolled (soaking, 1100°C, 2hr) in the temperature range of 1050-800°C in two passes ... followed by finally water quenching to room temperature from finish rolling temperature' [b0014]. The hot rolled & quenched (HRQ) state is a distinct studied specimen containing martensite [b0038].

unmapped_findings: The theoretical stacking fault energy (SFE) of the designed steel was calculated as ~35 mJ/m² (within the 20-40 mJ/m² TWIP range) using the Olson-Cohen thermodynamic model; the SFE of reverted austenite in the IA750_60 Min specimen was recalculated as ~27 mJ/m² based on its measured Mn (7.58 wt.%) and Al (3.96 wt.%) contents.

The developed steel density was measured as 6.91455 g/cc by Archimedes' principle, corresponding to a ~11.35% reduction relative to conventional steel (~7.8 g/cc), achieved by adding ~5 wt.% Al and ~1 wt.% Si.
No k-carbide precipitation was observed in the IA750_60 Min specimen; SEM, HRTEM and 3D atom probe tomography found no evidence of precipitates or elemental clustering.

APT atomic composition: reverted austenite contains Fe 72.92±0.33, Mn 12.41±0.24, Al 11.74±0.32, Si 1.34±0.08, C 1.59±0.09 (at.%); intercritical ferrite contains Fe 77.94±0.35, Mn 5.65±0.36, Al 14.41±0.14, Si 1.76±0.12, C 0.24±0.12 (at.%).
The martensite start temperature was calculated as ~350°C, supporting the transformation of austenite to lenticular martensite during water quenching from the finish rolling temperature (~800°C).

Tensile tests were performed at room temperature at a strain rate of 2.67×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ on ASTM E8/E8M subsize specimens machined along the rolling direction; nanoindentation was performed with a Berkovich tip at 30 mN load.

No TWIP effect was observed in the high-SFE alloy, and the plastic region of the stress-strain curves showed no serrations; the balance of size and chemical composition was concluded to determine the mechanical stability of the reverted austenite.
